summary: Instagram is doing nearly all the work: Hindi videos get 100 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts barely move (mostly under 30 views). The PIR motion sensor video is the clear winner, with the most views, likes, shares and saves on both platforms. The one English video got views only on YouTube and nothing on Instagram, and all videos are still very small, so these are early signals, not proof.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first, everyday-object sensor explainers. The best video takes a familiar device (motion sensor, street light) and opens with a surprising 'it does not actually do what you think' claim ('Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!'), followed by a 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' question title with the 🤔 emoji. Short curiosity-gap titles about things people see daily (street light, phone rotation, auto door) get the most saves and shares.
doMore: Open with a 'myth-breaking' line: 'X does not actually do Y' before explaining how it works
Pick sensors people meet daily (fan, lift, ATM, AC, car parking beeper) and name the device in the title
Post Instagram-first and test a few Hindi titles on YouTube with a stronger first-second visual
End each video with a save-worthy line or mini cheat sheet so saves and shares go up
Repeat the PIR format on close siblings: one hidden-sense reveal, one simple analogy, one real-life example
stopDoing: Publishing near-duplicate topics (two smoke detector videos, two IR/dark-sensing videos) that split the audience
Posting English videos with no Instagram version while the audience is responding to Hindi
Vague or generic titles that don't contain a surprising claim
nextTopics: Lift sensor: how the lift door stops when you put a hand
